(1) Existing datasets for 3D hand estimation are not generalizable, (2) we introduce the first dataset with 3D hand annotations that can be used to train a network for hand shape estimation from a single RGB view.

(1) existing datasets for 3D hand shape estimation do not generalize well to other datasets or to in the wild scenarios, (2) we introduce the FreiHAND dataset that is accompanied with annotations for both 3D pose estimation and shape estimation and (3) we show that the proposed dataset can serve as a good benchmark for both 3d hand pose and hand shape estimation

we introduce a novel large scale, multi-view dataset for markerless hand pose and shape estimation, and that our dataset is a good training ground for methods that estimate 3D hand poses and full hand shapes from single RGB images.

the following contributions: (i) a novel, semi automated annotation approach, (ii) a large scale, multi-view hand dataset with 3D hand shape annotations and (iii) a new benchmark for articulated hand reconstruction.

our dataset is a valuable resource for the community, and that it can be used as a benchmark for both 3D pose estimation and articulated hand shape estimation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a large scale, multi-view dataset that allows training of a single network that predicts both 3D pose, 3D shape and hand segmentation from a single RGB input.

we introduce a new, large scale hand dataset that is annotated with both 3D pose, 2D joints and 3D shape, we show that existing methods generalize poorly and we introduce a method to train a network for articulated hand shape prediction.
we present a new dataset, a new annotation approach and an analysis of cross dataset generalization for 3D hand reconstruction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lack of large scale, multi-view datasets that contain both 3D pose as well as 3D hand shape annotations, is the reason for the lack of generalization in existing approaches.
a new large scale, real world dataset is required to train models that are capable of estimating hand pose and shape robustly in real world scenarios.
training on a dataset that contains a large variety of hand poses and shapes is key to generalizable hand pose and shape estimation.
